text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam's Deputy Foreign Minister Nguyen Dinh Bin has held talks with U.S officials in Washington to discuss measures aimed at promoting relations.
-- Vietnam expects to see more technocrats and professional people in the National Assembly following nationwide elections to the legislature on July 20.
-- A Libyan foreign affairs delegation has visited Vietnam to promote relations between the two countries.
-- The National Assembly has approved new regulations allowing foreign firms in Vietnam to apply their own accounting practises.
-- The Government has proposed measures aimed at stepping up future disbursement of official development assistance (ODA).
-- Vietnam exported 270,000 tonnes of coffee in the first four months of 1997.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet told the U.S charge d'affaires it's important for both countries to have better understanding and mutual trust.
-- Vietnam reported an trade deficit of $962 million in the first four months of this year.
-- Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam is on a five-day visit to North Korea Korea to promote relations between the two countries.
-- Two police officers, suspected of involvement in the country's biggest drugs case, have been arrested.
